title: Cross-region stream coordinator switchover with session continuity and graceful shedding
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
Design and implement a coordinated cross-region switchover mechanism for the hosted API gateway that preserves streaming session continuity and honors SLOs during active-active failovers. We must support: sticky/transferable session tokens for long-lived streaming connections, coordinated KV-cache warming and prefix propagation, region-level circuit breakers, and deterministic load-shedding heuristics so critical low-latency requests maintain SLOs when capacity is constrained.

Goals / SLOs:
- For non-streaming generation: p50 <= 40ms, p95 <= 90ms, p99 <= 200ms under normal load; during regional degradation, maintain successful request rate >= 99.5% with tail-latency degradation bounded to +150ms.
- For streaming sessions: continuity SLO defined as "end-to-end stream without forced reconnect" >= 99.8% for single-region degradations; cross-region continuation allowed with a best-effort target >= 99.0%.
- Error budget rules: if sustained error-rate > 0.5% for 5m or p99 latency exceeds threshold for 3m then trigger regional circuit breaker and automated traffic shift policy.

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Session identity and handoff:
   - Issue a signed session token on connection establishment that contains: origin-region, session-version, last-kv-prefix, stream-offset (if streaming), and a replication-vector that tracks whether the session state has been replicated to other regions. Token format is compact JSON Web Token (JWT) with HMAC, short TTL and transparent rotation.
   - Implement a lightweight cross-region "handoff API" on the control plane that can accept a session token and return the minimal state required to resume streaming (KV prefixes, last message nonce, model cache hint). This API is rate-limited and intended only for failover resumption, not for live replication of every stream event.
2) KV cache warmers and prefix propagation:
   - Maintain per-session prefix lists keyed by session token. When a session is marked as eligible for cross-region continuation (replication-vector set), schedule asynchronous prefix propagation to nearest replica pools. Warmers will prioritize prefixes with highest access frequency.
   - Accept eventual consistency in prefix propagation; the handoff API will return missing prefixes as objects streamed from origin if not yet warmed.
3) Circuit breakers and shedding:
   - Region breaker evaluation based on combined signals: request error rate, p99 latency, GPU utilization, ingress queue length. Use hysteresis window 30s/3m to avoid flapping.
   - Load-shedding tiers: Tier 0 (critical system & internal health probes) -> Tier 1 (paid customers with high SLA flag) -> Tier 2 (standard customers) -> Tier 3 (free/trial). Code paths will drop or degrade lower-tier traffic first.
   - Shedding primitives: immediate 503 with Retry-After for cheap requests, partial-response heuristic for batch requests (return first N tokens), and synthetic early-termination with well-formed closing frames for streaming clients to avoid silent stalls.
4) Traffic shifting policy:
   - Gradual canary weights: 0% -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over configurable windows. Shift triggered automatically by breaker events or operator override.
   - Sticky sessions: by default route by session-token origin-region until the token's replication-vector indicates cross-region readiness or until regional breaker trips. On trip, session tokens are rehomed using handoff API.
5) Observability and SLO accountability:
   - New dashboards: per-region streaming continuity, session-handoff latency, prefix-warm hit-rate, handoff API error-rate, and load-shed counts by tier.
   - Alerting: SLO burn-rate alert at 50% and 90% with paging at 90% sustained for 10m.

Trade-offs and decisions made so far:
- Chosen token-based handoff over full active replication: reduces bandwidth and complexity at cost of occasional resume latency when prefixes are missing. We accepted an E2E best-effort continuity target for cross-region resumes to avoid doubling write throughput across regions.
- Preferring partial-response protocols for streaming termination rather than opaque silent disconnects to improve client debuggability; requires SDK updates to handle explicit short-circuit frames.
- Using JWT HMAC tokens rather than full KMS-signed tokens to avoid KMS QoS dependence during failovers; token compromise risk mitigated by short TTL and rotation.

Open implementation tasks:
- Server: implement /internal/handoff/v1 resume endpoint (ENG-61701 linked PR).
- Runtime: add session token parsing and resume logic into gateway pipeline (ENG-61702).
- Control-plane: prefix warmer service with eviction policy and priority queue (ENG-61703).
- Frontend SDK: add reconnection APIs and support for early-termination frames (RFC draft at Confluence).

Testing & rollout plan:
- Unit + integration tests for token parsing and handoff flows.
- Canary environment: run simulated cross-region failover test with 10k concurrent streams; verify continuity and latency metrics.
- Chaos exercises: automated region-emulation (packet loss, increased latency, AZ kill) to validate breaker behavior and shedding rules.
- Rollout: initial internal canary (1%) -> partner tenants (5%) -> public (25% then 100%) over 6 weeks, with rollback gates tied to SLO burn and error-rate thresholds.

- M2 (2026-03-31): gateway resume logic + SDK prototype for early-termination frames.
- M3 (2026-04-08): internal canary + chaos test report and decision to progress to partner canary.
